title: 01 Matrix
statement: For every cell return its distance to the nearest 0, counting steps between side-adjacent cells. Cells holding 0 have distance 0. At least one 0 is always present.
constraints: entries are 0 or 1, and at least one 0 exists
hints: A separate search starting from each 1 is correct and far too slow. Turn the search around.
Start from every 0 at once. Push all of them into the queue before the loop begins, and the first time a breadth-first search reaches a cell, that is its shortest distance.

This multi-source trick is the same one behind Rotting Oranges and Load Path to Ground. There is also a two-pass dynamic programming solution - sweep top-left to bottom-right, then bottom-right to top-left - which needs no queue at all.

cases.name: a row of 1s below the zeros
distance grows away from a lone corner zero
zero on the right of a single row
zeros at both ends meet in the middle
